problem_statement: Priya Nair's Astro developer portfolio has a clean personal-site shell — a fixed Home/Work/About nav, a hero, an about section with a skill row, a flat Projects grid, work history, and education — but the Projects grid is a single undifferentiated list. A visitor cannot tell the web work from the mobile apps from the platform tooling, and there is no way to narrow the grid by the kind of engineering each project took. Turn the Projects grid into a real WorkShelf: a stack-filterable card grid built from the existing project data, with a chip row (All / Web / Mobile / Platform) that re-filters the visible project cards and updates a live 'Showing N of 6 · <stack>' result count. Reuse the same WorkShelf control as the primary grid on a dedicated Work page and as a compact 'Selected work' rail on the About page, so the project story stays continuous across the three routes. Keep the existing light editorial identity: white surface, IBM-Plex-style monospace type, the blue #1d4ed8 accent, rounded gray-50 project cards with dark stack tags, and the centered fixed nav. The chip row and card grid must wrap cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow, the active chip must stay legible, cards must keep stable non-overlapping dimensions, and clicking a stack must actually filter the cards and update the count.
required_content: The Projects grid becomes a WorkShelf: a stack-filterable card grid built from the existing project data, with an All / Web / Mobile / Platform chip row and a live 'Showing N of 6 · <stack>' result count.
Clicking a stack chip re-filters the visible project cards and updates the count readout so it matches the cards shown (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 6 · Mobile').

The same WorkShelf control appears as the primary grid on a dedicated Work page and as a compact 'Selected work' rail on the About page, keeping the project story continuous across the Home, Work, and About routes.
The active stack chip stays legible against the light surface, and the project cards keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions consistent with the rounded gray-50 card treatment.
The existing nav, hero, about copy and skills, work history, and education remain available and unchanged in meaning.
The WorkShelf chip row and card grid have no horizontal overflow, clipped cards, or overlapping text at 390px.
design_constraints: Preserve the Priya Nair portfolio identity: white surface, monospace body type, the blue #1d4ed8 accent underline/active chip, rounded gray-50 project cards with subtle gray-200 borders and dark stack tags, and the centered fixed Home/Work/About nav.
Do not convert the personal portfolio into a bright SaaS landing page, a dashboard, or a marketing site; it must still feel like an individual engineer's editorial portfolio.
Build the WorkShelf from the existing project data and real stack metadata; do not invent unrelated stock content or filler.
Project cards must have restrained density, stable dimensions, readable metadata, and consistent border/radius treatment; the active filter chip must have legible contrast.
The chip row must wrap rather than force a fixed-width horizontal track that overflows narrow viewports.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the home hero, the Home/Work/About nav, the about copy and skills, and the WorkShelf project grid.
desktop_home_shelf scrolls the WorkShelf into view on Home: the All/Web/Mobile/Platform chip row, the live 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work' count, and the six project cards.
desktop_work captures the dedicated Work page whose primary grid is the same WorkShelf control (cross-route continuity).
desktop_about captures the About page with the compact 'Selected work' WorkShelf rail alongside the biography, work history, and education.
desktop_home_filter_mobile captures Home after clicking the Mobile stack chip: the grid re-filters to the two mobile projects and the count readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Mobile'.
mobile_initial, mobile_home_shelf, and tablet_home_shelf capture responsive states where the WorkShelf chip row and cards must wrap cleanly with no horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The Projects grid is a working WorkShelf with an All / Web / Mobile / Platform chip row and a live 'Showing N of 6 · <stack>' count.
Clicking a stack chip filters the visible cards and updates the count so it matches the cards actually shown (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 6 · Mobile').
The same WorkShelf is reused as the Work-page grid and a compact About rail for a continuous cross-route project story.
The existing nav, hero, about copy, skills, work history, and education remain available.
design_consistency: The WorkShelf matches the light monospace devportfolio system: white surface, blue #1d4ed8 accent, rounded gray-50 cards, gray-200 borders, and dark stack tags.
The active stack chip is legible and cards keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions.
The site remains a personal engineer's editorial portfolio rather than a generic dashboard or SaaS landing page.
responsive: Mobile and tablet home-shelf states have no horizontal overflow and keep all routes reachable.
The WorkShelf chip row and project cards wrap cleanly at 390px width without clipping or overlap.
regression: The Home/Work/About nav, hero, about section, skills row, work history, and education are not removed.
Project links still open externally and internal navigation between the three routes stays consistent.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro add/cross_page task on Priya Nair's RyanFitzgerald devportfolio, a light monospace developer portfolio. The native lever is the Projects grid's own stack filter — a WorkShelf chip row (All / Web / Mobile / Platform) that re-filters the project cards and updates a live 'Showing N of 6 · <stack>' result count, reused as the Work-page grid and a compact 'Selected work' About rail. Assets include the rounded gray-50 project cards, the blue #1d4ed8 accent, the /favicon.svg and bundled /_astro/ stylesheet, and the config-driven project data. L4 gates: no_horizontal_overflow (mobile chip row), visual_regression (WorkShelf layout + active-chip legibility), dom_assertions (cross-route WorkShelf presence), interaction_assertions (stack-chip re-filter + recount).
scope_note: cross_page: WorkShelf continuity across Home, Work, and About routes.
